facts.value: Psychoanalysis is a collection of theories and therapeutic techniques intended to analyze the unconscious mind and its impact on everyday life.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Psychoanalysis originated in the 1890s, most prominently with the work of Sigmund Freud.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Freud's psychoanalytic theory was largely based on interpretive methods, introspection, and clinical observation.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Psychoanalysis became very well known because it tackled subjects such as sexuality, repression, and the unconscious.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Freud pioneered the methods of free association and dream interpretation.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Other well-known psychoanalytic thinkers who diverged from Freud include Alfred Adler, Carl Jung, Erik Erikson, Melanie Klein, D. W. Winnicott, Karen Horney, Erich Fromm, John Bowlby, Freud's daughter Anna Freud, and Harry Stack Sullivan.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: These individuals ensured that psychoanalysis would evolve into diverse schools of thought such as ego psychology, object relations, interpersonal psychoanalysis, Lacanian psychoanalysis, and relational psychoanalysis.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Psychologists such as Hans Eysenck and philosophers including Karl Popper sharply criticized psychoanalysis.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Popper argued that psychoanalysis was not falsifiable and therefore inherently not a scientific discipline.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Eysenck advanced the view that experimental data had contradicted psychoanalytic tenets.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: By the end of the 20th century, psychology departments in American universities mostly had marginalized Freudian theory, dismissing it as a 'desiccated and dead' historical artifact.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Researchers such as António Damásio, Oliver Sacks, and Joseph LeDoux; and individuals in the emerging field of neuro-psychoanalysis have defended some of Freud's ideas on scientific grounds.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick
